content: coffee a controlled explosion on a film set near the O2 arena in London ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and a lorry. Firefighters were summoned to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday. After about an hour and with the effort of roughly twenty‑five crews, the blaze was brought under control and no injuries were reported. The incident is believed to have stemmed from a pre‑planned filming activity taking place close to the venue, which is slated to host performances by Niall Horan and Texas later in the week. The London Fire Brigade updated on X, stating that the fire in Silvertown is now contained, noting that one vehicle was lost while most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, and that there are currently no injury reports. They added that the blaze originated from a controlled explosion on the set that spread beyond expectations, prompting firefighters to act swiftly; crews will stay on site for the rest of the evening. The yard is situated near London’s cable‑car crossing over the River Thames. A Metropolitan Police spokesman said they are aware of reports of explosions heard in the area around the O2 in Greenwich.
